description: 4 exemplars + 4 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-08-30 under road-to-governed-harness-evolution 2.4, wave 1: this skill carries the highest inbound confusion count in the corpus (5 negatives in other skills' corpora name it as the correct destination) while carrying no corpus of its own. Exemplars cover the vulnerability hunt over EXISTING application code. Near-misses are the four neighbours that named it: the pre-implementation threat pass, the posture scorecard, the agent-config red-team, and host hardening.

queries.q: audit this codebase for injection vulnerabilities — SQLi, XSS, unsafe deserialization
do a pentest-style review of our application code and list what an attacker could actually reach
scan our dependencies for known CVEs and tell me which of them are reachable from our code
mach einen Security-Audit dieses Moduls und finde die Schwachstellen im Code
threat-model this new payments endpoint before I build it
queries.note: pre-implementation abuse-case pass over a change that does not exist yet, not a hunt through shipped code → threat-modeling

queries.q: give me an A-F security-maturity scorecard for this module with category ratings
queries.note: posture rating with evidence per category, explicitly not a vulnerability hunt → security-maturity-assessment

queries.q: red-team my agent config — could someone weaponise my CLAUDE.md or MCP servers?
queries.note: the attack surface is the agent's own configuration, not application code → agent-security-review

queries.q: harden this Ubuntu box — SSH posture and a default-deny firewall baseline
queries.note: operating-system posture on a host you run, verified on the box → server-hardening

queries.q: add a password strength meter to the signup form
queries.note: implementing a security-flavoured FEATURE; the word security appears and no audit is asked for

queries.q: why is this query slow — profile the hot path
queries.note: performance work with no security surface at all; guards against triggering on any 'audit this' phrasing
